title: Norway gas
subtitle: How Gassco's planned-maintenance end dates slip: 392 maintenances rebuilt from the public UMM archive, checked on physical flows, tested forward
headline: Norwegian gas maintenance ends on time when it is short and runs late 30% of the time when it is planned for one to three weeks (46 events, mean slip +5.4 days). The overrun is physical: exports fall on slipped days as on announced ones. A frozen forecast table is now being tested forward, day by day.

sections.title: What the archive shows
paragraphs: 392 completed planned maintenances on the Norwegian gas network, rebuilt revision by revision from Gassco's public messages (3,004 revisions). 73% ended exactly when announced at the start, 11% more than a day late, 5% more than a day early: late beats early 45 to 21 (sign test p = 0.004, the pre-registered hypothesis holds).
The slip lives in maintenance planned for one to three weeks. Short jobs are on time; the longest ones end early as often as late.

sections.title: By type of asset
paragraphs: Fields, processing plants (Kårstø, Kollsnes, Nyhamna...) and exit terminals behave alike on the share late; the means are driven by a few long overruns.

sections.title: The slip is physical
paragraphs: Daily Norwegian export flows (ENTSOG, 2024-12 to 2026-11) regressed on unavailable capacity, each maintenance split into the days announced at its start and the days it slipped. A mcm/d of slipped capacity removes 4.7 GWh/d of exports, a mcm/d announced 3.3: the extra days are real outages, not paperwork. Pre-registered before it was run; it holds in every robustness check.

sections.title: Can the slip be predicted?
paragraphs: Out of sample (208 events before 2026, 184 in 2026), no correction beats the announced date as a point estimate (the second hypothesis fails): mean absolute error 0.98 days trusting the message. What is predictable is the risk around the date, by planned duration. That is what the forward test now checks.

sections.title: Next 30 days, in aggregate
paragraphs: 4 planned maintenances are running or start within 30 days (2 running now). Announced unavailable capacity peaks at 47 mcm/d on 2026-11-24. Applied to each of them, the frozen table expects 0.8 to come back more than a day late, most of that risk in the maintenances planned for over 3 weeks.
Event by event figures stay off this page until Gassco's terms on republication are confirmed.

sections.title: Forward test, live since 13 November 2026
paragraphs: The forecast table was frozen and its SHA-256 committed (addendum 2 to the pre-registration). Every day the tool logs its forecast for each active maintenance: 174 forecasts over 1 day so far. Maintenances that begin after the freeze are scored once they end: 0 measured, 173 running or to come.
Primary test: do one-to-three-week maintenances still run late more often than short ones (one-sided Fisher)? Decided once, at 15 such events or on 2027-06-30. Until then the figures are interim.

ideas.title: Plan for slip on maintenance planned for 1 to 3 weeks
ideas.instrument: Supply balance and prompt/month-ahead position around the return date
ideas.condition: a planned outage of 7 to 21 days is announced
ideas.thesis: 30% of them ran more than a day late; one in five ran 5 days or more past the date.

ideas.title: After one extension, expect another
ideas.instrument: Return date of a maintenance already extended
ideas.condition: Gassco has pushed the end date back once
ideas.thesis: 38% of maintenances extended once were extended again, 47% after two, against 20% extended at all.

ideas.title: Take short maintenance dates as firm
ideas.instrument: Outages planned for two days or less
ideas.condition: a planned outage of 2 days or less is announced
ideas.thesis: Only 3.1% ran more than a day late. The message itself gives little warning when one does: 43% of all extensions come under 24 hours before the due date.

method: Each rule comes from the archive study: the announcement in force when the outage began against the final end date. Intervals: bootstrap by asset and year, 4,000 draws. Hypotheses and thresholds were committed before any statistic was computed.
caveats: Two seasons of data (maintenance from November 2024): 392 events, 46 of them planned for one to three weeks. The forward test is there to confirm it.
An end date nobody revises counts as on time: Gassco closes most events at the announced date.
Gassco publishes only events above 5 mcm/d; field and processing-plant outages can overlap, so summed volumes overstate the net loss.
No price test yet: it waits for a licensed daily TTF series.
Aggregates only. Gassco's terms say nothing about republication, so no event, asset or message is listed here; the code repository stays private until they are confirmed.
Data: Gassco AS (umm.gassco.no), which disclaims responsibility for the correctness and timeliness of the information; ENTSOG transparency platform. Not investment advice.
